highlights.title: Grand Theft Auto VI exists in its own universe
highlights.summary: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on GTA VI and the state of the video game industry, follow Andrew Webster. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started.
body: Rockstar’s latest epic is almost here, and it seems nothing can stop it.

Four years ago, fans got a long-awaited look at Grand Theft Auto VI with a huge cache of videos that showed off Rockstar’s latest open-world epic. There were 90 videos in total, providing a glimpse at the next-generation take on Vice City, introducing the game’s new dual protagonists, and generally showing off the crime-fueled mayhem the series is known for. The twist? This wasn’t some official reveal. The videos were part of a massive leak in September 2022 that ultimately ended with a life sentence in a secure hospital for the hacker, and they dropped months before Rockstar properly unveiled GTA VI to the world with its debut trailer.

highlights.title: Harvard’s $699 startup bootcamp offers AI avatars of its instructors
highlights.summary: In the HBS Foundry program, AI avatars provide feedback during practice pitches and board meetings.
body: As Harvard Business School seeks to expand its reach, it’s leaning on AI avatars to provide individual feedback.

New York Times reporter Sarah Kessler actually tried this out herself by pitching an AI-generated copy of Flybridge Capital co-founder Jeff Bussgang. Apparently, both the real Bussgang and his simulacra were unimpressed by her plan to build “Uber for bananas,” but Kessler said the virtual version offered a noticeably frozen smile during her pitch.

Project director Katharina Rings said she initially envisioned the AI component as something closer to a chatbot. However, after HBS released a trial version, students said they wanted a more guided experience.

And while some college students haven’t been shy about expressing their negative feelings towards AI, Foundry participants told Kessler they like the avatars. As for Bussgang, he acknowledged his digital copy is a little “creepy,” but he said, “My students love it.”

highlights.title: Lopez takes Romero's WBA title to become three-weight champion
highlights.summary: Teofimo Lopez beat Rolly Romero in Las Vegas on Saturday night to capture the WBA welterweight title and become a three-division world champion.
body: In his welterweight debut, Lopez secured a majority decision over his friend and sparring partner at the T-Mobile Arena. One judge scored the bout 114-114, while the other two had it 115-113 and 116-112 for Lopez.
It was an impressive return to form from Lopez after his loss to Shakur Stevenson in their WBO super lightweight title fight in January.

"I need to tell you guys, if you lose and you come back, then you never lost because you're a winner," Lopez said afterwards. "I'm a winner. I'm a true example of what winning is, and it ain't about losing. It's about never giving up."

In what was Romero's first appearance since taking the WBA title in an upset decision over Ryan Garcia in May 2025, he landed just 73 of 352 punches thrown, according to Compubox. Lopez landed 124 of 530 total punches.

highlights.title: Miyazaki explains how The Duskbloods plans to protect newcomers from its best players
highlights.summary: FromSoftware is stepping into one of multiplayer gaming's most divisive arguments with The Duskbloods, confirming the upcoming Switch 2 exclusive will lean on skill-based matchmaking to keep newcomers safe from its most battle-hardened players.
body: Speaking to IGN, FromSoftware president and Duskbloods director Hidetaka Miyazaki confirmed the game will run on a ranked system, pairing highly skilled players together and keeping newer players in their own pool specifically to avoid lopsided matches as the game's skill gap widens over time.

Skill-based matchmaking has been a persistent flashpoint in multiplayer games for years. Games like Call of Duty and Apex Legends have repeatedly faced backlash from players who feel it makes lobbies feel unnecessarily punishing.

"In terms of really, really good players, we definitely plan on having the matchmaking system work in a way so that it's ranked, and players who are really good tend to be matched with other players who are great, and players who are new tend to be matched with other new players just to avoid situations like you had mentioned," he explained.

highlights.summary: Nostalgia, like ecstasy, is a hell of a drug and Kieron J. Walsh’s warm-hearted, hot-headed “Skintown” is buzzing on both. A more polite brother to the “Kneecap” boys and a more cautious cousin to those “Derry Girls” still, the Fermanagh-set friendship comedy sends fizzy, sweetly chemical energy…
body: Against the backdrop of the 1994 IRA ceasefire, two friends land a score that could buy their ticket out of Northern Ireland in Kieron J. Walsh's Edinburgh Film Festival-winning charmer.

Still, as soon as Vinny gets the money together, he’s resolved to leave, although there are things he’ll miss: his supportive, hardworking paramedic mum (Roisin Gallagher); his peppy unrequited crush Eileen (Jamie Lee O’Donnell); and most of all, his best mate Jonty (Chris Walley), a shell-suited, high-spirited raver just out to have a good time. Vinny and Jonty are as thick as the thieves they eventually, inadvertently become when they’re pressganged into a caper involving a load of ecstasy stolen from the UVF (a loyalist paramilitary group).

highlights.title: How to make the perfect zaru soba, or cold soba noodles – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect
highlights.summary: Hot days call for cool dinners, and these are Japan’s nutty, salty and sweet solution. Fiery or pickled accompaniments optional. Although every culture craves something different in hot weather – chilled beetroot soup in Lithuania, cooling buttermilk drinks in India, gazpacho in Spain – what many…
body: Zaru soba isn’t the only chilled noodle dish that Japan slurps in summer – Emiko Davies favours her mother’s somen (delicate wheat-flour strands), while Shota Nakajima makes a case for hiyashi chuka, a Chinese-inspired ramen salad. Sadly, though, spindly somen and fresh ramen are trickier to source in the UK than buckwheat soba, which can be found in many larger supermarkets.

Once cooled, the soba are best consumed immediately, but if you find they’ve started to tangle, give them a rinse under cold water to separate the strands, then drain them well again afterwards. Traditionally, soba are served on a flat bamboo straining mat called a zaru, but as long as you toss them well, a less picturesque plate or bowl is fine.

The proper way to eat zaru soba, according to Maehashi, is to “pick up a few strands of noodles and dip only the bottom half of them into the dipping sauce by simply lowering the chopsticks. Many people drop all the noodles they just picked up into the dipping sauce,” she adds, “but this is not a real gourmet way of eating buckwheat noodles. By dipping only part of the soba noodles in, you can taste the flavour of the noodles and enjoy it better.” So that’s you told.

highlights.title: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
highlights.summary: Built by DeepMind alumni, British AI lab Inherent released Faraday, an AI agent whose ability to replicate scientific papers could be a stepping stone for innovation.
body: Inherent, a London AI lab founded by Google DeepMind alumni, says its AI agent just outperformed much larger models from Anthropic and OpenAI using a fraction of the size.

Of all the startups launched by Google DeepMind alumni, Inherent has gotten relatively little attention. But while better-funded rivals have yet to show the world anything concrete, the London-based team is starting to share what it’s been building.

Just weeks after emerging from stealth with a $50 million seed round, the British startup says its newly released AI agent, Faraday, has outperformed larger, better-known models at a specific task: independently reproducing the findings of published scientific papers without being told the answer in advance.

That may sound like a mere party trick given Inherent’s much loftier goal — building AI that can discover new scientific knowledge and not just verify old results. But paper replication is a standard training exercise for human scientists, too, cofounder and chief scientist Edward Hughes said. “Many PhD students actually start by doing this.”

highlights.title: Australia hammer Bangladesh inside two days to tie Test series
highlights.summary: Australia responded to their shock opening loss to Bangladesh in Darwin with a thumping innings victory inside two days in Mackay to tie the two-Test series at 1-1.
body: Mitchell Starc took 4-39 to finish with match figures of 10-51 as Bangladesh ​were dismissed for less than 100 for the second time in the match.
Pat Cummins also claimed 3-10 and off-spinner Nathan Lyon 3-25 as Bangladesh were bowled out for 95 in 38.3 overs before tea on day two.
That followed their first-innings 64 all out, and though Australia themselves managed only a score of 210, that ultimately proved plenty as they wrapped up an innings-and-51-run victory.
"Much better week," Starc, who was named Player of the Match, said. "We knew we weren't at our best, or what we expect of ourselves, in Darwin.

highlights.title: Sony sends PlayStation users a reminder they don't own their digital games just as a fan boycott over ending discs kicks off
highlights.summary: PlayStation users have received an unprompted reminder of exactly what they do and don't own on the platform, days before a planned boycott over Sony's decision to end new PlayStation discs from 2028.
body: "For your convenience and future reference, we have included full copies of the Terms in this email. Please retain this email for your records."

Several recipients said they'd received the email despite not touching their PS4 or PS5 in months. Rather than linking out to the full terms, the email reproduced each referenced document in full, including the section of the Software EULA covering digital purchases.

"The Software is licensed to you, not sold," it reads. "You are granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, and personal license to play or use the Software for your private, non-commercial use on the system or device it was intended for." The terms go on to restrict things like renting, modifying, or obtaining games through unauthorised means.

The email comes just as an attempted PlayStation boycott gets underway. Organised by fan group DoesItPlay, the #PSBlackout campaign runs from 23rd to 30th August and asks participants to log off, avoid purchases, and cancel subscriptions in protest at Sony's move away from physical media.

highlights.title: Stores are selling Halloween stuff in August. Time has lost all meaning | Dave Schilling
highlights.summary: Capitalism and the climate crisis are conspiring to destroy the concept of seasons. I’ll take solace in my pumpkin spice. Happy spooky season, everyone! Get those jack-o’-lanterns out, because Halloween is just around the corner! Just kidding, no, it’s not.
body: It’s August, for God’s sake. Every day, I wake up to 90F weather – my skin moist with sweat and my eyelids stuck together. I can’t drink coffee on my porch without being consumed by an army of voracious mosquitoes that seem to find my blood to be the most delicious of all.

Why am I fuming about this? Even though I love Halloween, I’m mad because our glorious big-box overlords have declared, via careful inventory selection, that Halloween season has begun. In August. I find all of that unacceptable. It feels like a violation of the natural order, a realignment of one of the few glorious constants left in the world. I yearn to go back to the tidy order of holidays, where no two ever cross paths. At most, Halloween celebrations should start in late September. Not a month after Independence Day. I fear those days are done, that our world has irrevocably changed and I need to start getting ready to give in to the new normal.

highlights.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
highlights.summary: OpenAI is calling for California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety bill that the company previously opposed.
body: OpenAI is calling for California to add more safeguards to a landmark AI safety bill that was passed last year.

In a LinkedIn post from the company’s global affairs team, OpenAI said California’s SB 53 “should be amended to expand safeguards,” for example by “requiring monitoring of frontier models under training or evaluation for potential serious incidents,” and by “strengthening cybersecurity protections throughout the model-development lifecycle.”
“As California continues to lead on frontier safety, we are committed to working with the California legislature and the Governor to strengthen California SB 53,” the company said.

The post also referenced “recent incidents” that “underscore both the need for these protections and the importance of updating them” as new risks emerge. Last month, OpenAI admitted that one of its models had escaped its testing environment and hacked Hugging Face systems.
points: OpenAI is calling for California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety bill that the company previously opposed.

highlights.title: HBO Max's New 9/10 Hardcore Thriller Is an Unforgettable Modern Cult Classic
highlights.summary: There are a surprising number of holiday-themed slasher movies, but horror hasn’t treated all holidays equally. Christmas and Halloween are vastly overrepresented, Valentine's Day and New Year's have a couple of dedicated films apiece, and Mexican horror gives the Day of the Dead the love you’d…
body: Specifically, there aren't that many slasher movies with a Thanksgiving theme, whether it's American or Canadian. There are several that happen to take place around Thanksgiving, like Wes Craven's Deadly Friend, but only a couple of horror films really do anything with the holiday proper. For years, the "Thanksgiving slasher" as a category only really had two movies in it: 1987's Blood Rage ("That ain't cranberry sauce!") and 1981's Home Sweet Home. If you were looking to put together a themed holiday horror marathon, which has come up more often than you might think, those were your options.

That was part of the joke behind Eli Roth's Thanksgiving, which debuted as one of the faux trailers shown during Quentin Tarantino and Robert Rodriguez's 2007 double feature Grindhouse. It was goofy as a concept and in execution, featuring a serial killer dressed as a Pilgrim, three separate decapitations, a memorable sequence involving a trampoline, and a real gross-out set at a family's dinner table.

highlights.title: Walking the Peak District, I discovered a wonderful rejection of the right’s monotone vision of England | John Harris
highlights.summary: The landscape was striking, but so was the diversity of the hikers. We can make this the new normal – and we should. A fortnight or so ago, my two teenage kids and I set out on a three-night visit to the Peak District where temperatures were hovering at a comparatively tepid 28C.
body: The next bit might sound self-parodically Guardian-esque, but what the hell: in its own way, the most striking sight was the diversity of the scores of people rambling up, down and along. Women in their 20s wearing hijabs picnicked on giant rocks, while multiracial gaggles of young men attempted to race to the top; solo and shirtless white fitness freaks and retirement-age dog walkers took their places alongside them. With plenty of justification, country walking has long been typified as one of the most monoculturally white pursuits there is. But here – presumably because of the relatively close proximity of Manchester and Sheffield – things looked different.

highlights.title: Volcanoes that made history
highlights.summary: The first telegram arrived in Singapore on a Monday, sent from the city of Batavia in the Dutch East Indies (now Jakarta, Indonesia). “Terrific detonations from Krakatau (volcanic island),” it reported. Soon afterward: “Stones falling.
body: Within days, the source of the destruction was known worldwide. On the morning of August 27, 1883, a volcanic eruption had obliterated two islands in the strait between Java and Sumatra, and most of a third. More than 36,000 people perished, the majority in devastating tsunamis that raced outward from the colossal explosion.

Thanks to Victorian-era telecommunications, it was the first time in history that people around the globe could begin to document, in near real time, the immediate and long-term effects of a catastrophic volcanic eruption. What they learned over the next few years laid the foundations for the modern science of volcanology. And it was an especially eye-opening lesson in how the biggest eruptions can influence climate, agriculture, and even the course of human history.

In the months after Krakatau, drifting volcanic particles high in the atmosphere circled the globe, causing violently colored sunsets that contemporary artists captured in paintings, likely including the psychedelic background of Edvard Munch’s The Scream.

highlights.title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
highlights.summary: A new study finds leading AI labs have few publicly documented plans for containing rogue models, raising questions about preparedness as AI systems increasingly demonstrate unexpected and potentially dangerous behavior.
body: Few of the top AI labs have published or demonstrated containment response plans, according to a recent study. A containment plan spells out what happens once an AI is caught trying to subvert human control — what access gets cut, and when the system gets shut down entirely.

That’s the finding from Guidelight AI Standards, an organization dedicated to promoting safe frontier AI development practices, which graded five leading labs on how prepared they are for exactly this scenario. OpenAI came out on top; Anthropic and Meta scored lowest. The findings matters as agentic AI takes on more autonomous roles inside companies’ own systems, and as regulators in California and New York begin requiring disclosure. For anyone building on or investing in these models, it’s a rare independent read on how seriously each lab treats operational risk versus how it talks about it.

highlights.title: Arc Raiders' fifth Expedition will be its last until early 2027
highlights.summary: Embark Studios has confirmed that Arc Raiders ' fifth Expedition, opening next month, will be the last one players see until early 2027.
body: "We have been carefully reviewing your feedback on Expeditions, and while we've made ongoing improvements along the way, we've come to realise that some of the issues you've raised, like the tight departure windows, the reward structure, and accessibility for new players, need more than incremental fixes," Embark said in a blog post. "They call for bigger changes."

The update added: "In order to address those concerns, we need to pause the Expeditions for a while. The fifth Expedition will be the last one until early 2027, when Expeditions will return with major improvements, tackling some of the biggest player pain points. So, if you've been on the fence about departing - now is the time! We will share more details on what those changes will look like in September."

The Expedition Window opens on 8th September and closes on 29th September, giving three weeks rather than the previous two. Quest progress reset, previously mandatory, is now opt-in for players who'd rather keep their quest line going than start over, though the Hullcracker Blueprint (normally tied to that quest line) will need an alternative route to unlock as a result.

This summer, UK web searches for “Hugo spritz”, an elderflower-flavoured aperitif, overtook searches for “Aperol spritz” for the first time.
body: Traditionally, the spritz is an Italian cocktail made from prosecco, a bitter aperitif or liqueur, and a splash of soda water to keep things steady. While Venetian bartenders are more likely to judge it by eye, there is a simple 3-2-1 formula for making a spritz at home: three parts prosecco, two parts liqueur and one part soda water. I’ve gone with 75ml/50ml/25ml – keep the same ratios to make a smaller (60ml/40ml/20ml) or larger (90ml/60ml/30ml) drink. Of course, you can then adjust it to make it stronger or weaker (I have been known to leave out the soda …).

If wine-based cocktails aren’t to your taste, shandy is also showing signs of a resurgence – Ocado sales have increased 40% year on year, and the craft brand Shandy Shack is now stocked in M&S. Being half beer, half soft drink, it is another summery thirst-quencher that is easy to make at home and (in theory) shouldn’t get you too sloshed.
So, here are 20 simple spritzes and shandies. Save your Malibu for a piña colada.
All recipes make one drink. Pour the liquids into a large glass with ice, stir briefly and garnish.

body: Laptops are ideal for getting work done when you're out and about, but if you need the functionality of a full workstation, being hunched over a small, flat keyboard can quickly get annoying. However, connecting your laptop to a secondary monitor, a mouse, and a comfier keyboard can turn your desk space into a nest of tangled cables. Not to mention that many of today's laptops are designed to be as thin as possible and don't have the ports you may need to connect some peripherals. That's when it's time to get a laptop docking station.

Laptop docking stations are small boxes that sit on your desk and stay connected to your monitor (or monitors) and peripherals such as speakers, a keyboard, or a mouse. With the right docking station, you can enjoy the portability of a laptop with the flexibility and features of a desktop. These stations can get expensive, though, and it's hard to figure out which to buy based on a list of ports or specs. I've tested many of the most popular options and whittled the list down to the best laptop docking stations for various use cases.

highlights.title: The Unlikely Place at the Center of China’s AI Boom
highlights.summary: Cheap energy, abundant land, and proximity to Beijing have turned a city in Inner Mongolia into a crucial hub for data centers.
body: Travel just two hours west of Beijing by train, and you’ll find yourself surrounded by the rolling grasslands and ancient cinder cones of Inner Mongolia. This vast, arid land has long been China’s capital of sheep farming and coal mining, but over the last few years, it has become the hottest place in the country to build an AI data center.

In Ulanqab, a city in Inner Mongolia home to about 1.5 million people, nearly 100 data centers have been opened or begun construction since 2016. Chinese companies have pledged to build projects with a combined estimated capacity of 12.5 gigawatts in the city, and over 70 percent of the total commitments have been announced in just the last year, making it one of the fastest growing compute clusters in Asia, according to a research note published by Goldman Sachs last week. For comparison, OpenAI’s $500 billion Stargate Project is set to reach only 10 gigawatts of total capacity when it’s complete.

highlights.title: D&D's New Hardcore Setting Fixes the Game's Most Iconic Monster
highlights.summary: If you are a Dungeons & Dragons Dungeon Master, it’s very likely that, at one point, you’ve either put a dragon in one of your games or at least considered it. It’s right there in the title, after all.
body: That’s the problem with iconic monsters: they’re everywhere. Dragons are one of the foundations of the western fantasy genre, and it’s fair to say that they have lost some of their mystique. D&D actually does a good job of keeping them interesting, with the different varieties offering more options for DMs, but at the end of the day, a dragon is still a dragon. A big, scary monster that flies, breathes some kind of deadly substance, and likes shiny things. Except in one place: Athas, the world where the Dark Sun setting takes place.

During Gen Con 2026, D&D shared many exciting news with its fans. One of them was the return of one of the most fascinating settings in the game’s long history: the brutal Dark Sun, a “Mad Max meets grimdark” world ravaged by deadly magic where survivors fight for their freedom against godlike wizard tyrants. And of course, there’s no shortage of monsters to be found.

In Athas, dragons are extremely rare — as they should be. One of the most important characters in Dark Sun is Borys of Ebe, also known as The Dragon, because he’s the only one in the entire world. In Athas, dragons aren’t born. They are made.

highlights.title: Clash Royale research finds 85% of rage quitters enjoy gaming more after returning
highlights.summary: Supercell has revealed that 85.1% of rage quitters say they enjoy gaming more when they come back. That's according to research commissioned by Clash Royale, which surveyed 9,000 gamers across seven markets as the mobile game searches for a player to become its first-ever rage emote.... [ MORE ]
body: The research found that Mexico had the highest share of players who enjoyed the game more after returning from a rage quit, at 90.5%, while Germany recorded the lowest at 74.4%.

Globally, gamers said they rage quit because they want to do well (31.1%), care about the game (22.1%) and want to protect a winning streak (21.9%). Brazil had the highest share of gamers who had rage quit, at 77%, compared with 59% in Mexico.

The research also found that close to four in 10 gamers who rage quit have done so somewhere public. The US was the only market where gamers wanted an audience, with 55.6% of US rage quitters saying they would happily post a clip of the moment.
In the UK, 31.5% of public rage quitters had done so in a pub, while British gamers also led in ranting to a friend at 20.8% and screaming into a pillow at 17.2%.

body: MoreThan Films has acquired Colombian filmmaker Sebastián Múnera ‘s film “Meteorite,” which will have its world premiere in Venice Critics’ Week (Sept. 2-12).

Queralt Pons Serra, managing partner at MoreThan Films, said, “What excited us about ‘Meteorite’ from the beginning was the strength and singularity of Sebastián’s gaze. You can really feel his artistic background in the way he approaches images, spaces and textures, creating a world that is incredibly cinematic, beautiful and also deeply emotional. There is something very immersive and atmospheric about the film that stayed with us long after watching it.”

Múnera is a Colombian visual artist and filmmaker. He was a resident at the Cité Internationale des Arts in Paris, invited by the Centre Georges Pompidou. His films have been selected at festivals such as IFFR Rotterdam, DOK Leipzig and FICCI Cartagena. He has received distinctions including the Humberto Solás Cine en Construcción Award and the International Symposium on Auteur Cinema Altiplano Incuba Award.
“Meteorite,” his first fiction feature, was awarded at work-in-progress programs in Málaga and Cartagena.

body: I’ve always liked Miami best with a little room to spread out. I grew up coming here on family vacations, then came back for solo escapes, girls’ trips, and romantic weekends by the beach. Somehow, I still find myself falling for the city’s distinct combination of pastel Art Deco buildings, swaying palm trees, warm ocean air, and vibrant neighborhoods that feel like their own little universes.

Hotels can of course be fabulous here, but there’s something especially fun about having your own Miami address for a few days. A Miami Airbnb gives you the space to make coffee in your pajamas, open the doors to a pool or garden, pile everyone onto a sofa after the beach, and actually unpack instead of living out of a suitcase. I’m talking a leafy Coconut Grove hideaway, a glossy Brickell apartment with skyline views, or a colorful family house with a pool that has the potential to make leaving for dinner feel like a chore.
These are the Airbnbs I'd genuinely want to stay at in Miami—from breezy beach bases to character-filled homes that make a weekend away feel like a proper escape.

body: LinkedIn’s new AI slop button is apparently getting a lot of use.

LinkedIn announced the button a few weeks after AI detector Pangram determined that 41 percent of LinkedIn’s longform posts were flagged as fully AI generated, which 404 Media reported on. Alongside the AI slop button, LinkedIn introduced “new and improved” classifiers to identify posts as AI and removed a feature that would “enhance your post” with AI.

“AI slop is a top priority for all of us,” Srinivasan said at the time, and it sounds as if the platform’s changes may be making a difference. In Thursday’s post, Srinivasan said that users are overall “now experiencing 40% less views on what we classify as AI slop from just a few weeks ago.”
LinkedIn is also adding a new message that will tell users who make a post if “Some members told us this post seems like AI.”

highlights.title: Is Expensive Bottled Water Actually Better for You?
highlights.summary: Luxury water can contain different minerals and taste noticeably different. But a remote source, alkaline pH, and high price do not necessarily mean better hydration.
body: Water is supposed to be the simplest thing we consume. The premium bottled water industry has transformed it into something that requires a backstory.

Supermarket shelves now distinguish between glacial, iceberg, volcanic, spring, mineral, and alkaline water. Restaurants are introducing water menus, while trained water sommeliers assess bottles by their mineral composition, mouthfeel and provenance. At the extreme end of the category, Svalbarði Polar Iceberg Water sells Arctic water for as much as €100 (around $116) a bottle.

The category’s growth rests on a mixture of verifiable differences and carefully constructed associations. Water can contain different minerals. Those minerals can change how it tastes. But claims about purity, alkaline pH, and remote natural sources can also create the impression that expensive water must be healthier.
points: Luxury water can contain different minerals and taste noticeably different.
But a remote source, alkaline pH, and high price do not necessarily mean better hydration.
The premium bottled water industry has transformed it into something that requires a backstory.
At the extreme end of the category, Svalbarði Polar Iceberg Water sells Arctic water for as much as €100 (around $116) a bottle.
